bear_case: The session produced three simultaneous warning signals that share a structural root: (1) NVDA Gate 3 failed for the fourth consecutive time as NQ rebalancing sold existing constituents to fund SPCX, (2) KOSPI triggered a circuit breaker (-8.22% intraday) on leveraged ETF forced selling, and (3) BTC failed the $64K push while the Coinbase Premium extended its record 50-day negative streak. The common thread: mechanical and systematic forces (NQ rebalancing, leveraged ETF feedback loops, spot-vs-ETF divergence) are dominating price action in AI semiconductors and crypto. These mechanisms work in reverse equally well: a hawkish FOMC minutes tomorrow (June dot plot: 9/18 officials for rate hike) could trigger VIX above 17 — which simultaneously invalidates the dual-gate regime, pressures NVDA toward the $195 stop threshold, and tests BTC's $62,000 Gate 2 floor. The 30Y yield crossing above 5.00% is the new regime risk signal on the table. If sustained above 5% through July 28 FOMC, the implied discount rate for NVDA's $91B earnings guide and BTC's store-of-value thesis both compress materially. The circuit-breaker KOSPI session and SPCX's 29% inclusion-day crash are the clearest signals that the July 7 session was structurally dislocated, not trend-defining — but the FOMC minutes tomorrow will determine whether it was a one-day anomaly or the start of a new down phase.
